title: What Is a Twitch Affiliate? How To Make Money on Twitch
summary: If you meet the platform’s minimum requirements, you can join the Twitch Affiliate and start earning from your livestreams.
body_markdown:
Becoming a Twitch affiliate begins with building an audience. For some, it can turn livestreaming on Twitch from a hobby into a source of income. Streamers can earn money through subscriptions, ads, sponsorships, and other opportunities, but getting paid through Twitch requires Affiliate or Partner status.


For many newer creators, becoming a Twitch Affiliate is an important early milestone on the path toward monetizing a channel.


According to[TwitchTracker](https://twitchtracker.com/statistics/active-streamers?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , there are 1.1 million streamers broadcasting content on the platform daily. Standing out in that environment takes work. Achieving Twitch Affiliate status can help you distinguish your channel by unlocking additional community-building tools, such as subscriptions and Channel Points. These give viewers more ways to engage with your stream and become regular members of your[primary audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/primary-audience) .


Learn more about the Twitch Affiliate program, including how streamers earn money and the benefits of becoming an affiliate. Pick up streaming tips to help grow your account, reach affiliate program eligibility, and discover other ways to[make money as a Twitch streamer](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-make-money-on-twitch) .


## What is a Twitch Affiliate?


Twitch Affiliates are verified streamers approved by Twitch. Joining the[affiliate marketing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/affiliate-marketing) program allows creators to earn income from their content. Affiliate streamers have access to monetization tools and customization options unavailable to standard accounts. Benefits include:


-


**Subscriptions.** Affiliates can offer paid channel subscriptions with exclusive viewer benefits.


-


**Bits.** Affiliates can earn income from Bits, a digital good available for purchase on Twitch. Viewers award Bits by cheering during streams, and the creator can eventually convert them into cash.


-


**Ad revenue.** Affiliates can earn a portion of ad revenue associated with their streams. For affiliates, Twitch offers a standard 50/50 revenue split.


-


**Channel points.** Affiliates can design custom channel points programs to reward loyal viewers for watching and participating in streams.


-


**Extended video-on-demand storage.** Affiliate channels can display past livestreams for 14 days. Standard accounts are only granted seven days of storage.


The[affiliate program](https://www.shopify.com/blog/best-affiliate-programs) is Twitch’s entry-level monetization program. Twitch also has a higher-tier program, the Twitch Partnership program, designed for larger channels. Partnership has enhanced benefits, like 60-day VOD storage and a more favorable ad revenue split.


The affiliate program is available to small streamers who meet a few simple requirements, while partnership is slightly more exclusive.

## Twitch Affiliate Program requirements


Streamers must meet four basic requirements to become eligible for the Twitch Affiliate Program. According to[Twitch policies](https://help.twitch.tv/s/article/joining-the-affiliate-program?language=en_US#becoming) , affiliates must:


-


Reach a minimum of 25 followers


-


Stream for a minimum of four hours


-


Stream on four different days


-


Reach an average of three concurrent viewers per stream on four different days


You can track your progress towards eligibility in the achievements section of your Twitch Creator Dashboard. Twitch will invite you to join the affiliate program once your account meets the requirements.


After receiving an invitation, creators must enable[two-factor authentication](https://www.shopify.com/blog/payment-security) , fill out the account details page, and accept the Twitch Monetized Streamer Agreement to complete the affiliate onboarding process.

## Tips for becoming a Twitch Affiliate


- Choose a niche
- Stream consistently
- Cross-promote on other social channels
- Focus on engagement and community


The requirements may sound straightforward, but that doesn’t mean becoming a Twitch Affiliate is easy. Honing your unique voice,[building an audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/audience-growth-strategy) , and committing to regular streams can help your channel gain the views and followers you need to reach affiliate status. Here’s how:


### Choose a niche


Twitch averages more than 1 million streams every day. The abundance of content can make it difficult for new channels to break through. Popular categories like Just Chatting, Minecraft, and Counter-Strike attract a lot of viewers, but they also already have plenty of options.


If you stream in a top category, you’ll be fighting against well-established channels with thousands of viewers.[Choosing a less saturated niche](https://www.shopify.com/blog/6187532-dont-follow-your-passion-a-smarter-way-to-find-a-product-to-sell) and[developing a unique personal voice](https://www.shopify.com/blog/new-rules-of-brand-voice) can help your channel stand out.


### Stream consistently


Establishing a streaming schedule can help your channel attract regular viewers. If you always go live around the same time of day or on the same days, you can start to build a connection with viewers who are regularly active at that time.


Users will become familiar with your schedule and know when they can tune in to your content. Consistency can help your account reach affiliate status and put you on the path to becoming a Twitch partner.


### Cross-promote on other social channels


Use your other social media accounts to direct viewers over to Twitch. Announce your streams before you go live so that your followers know when to watch. You can also clip and repurpose old streams into content that can be shared across platforms.


For instance, Twitch makes it easy to share content on YouTube. If you connect your accounts, you can export videos directly to[a YouTube channel](https://www.shopify.com/blog/start-a-youtube-channel-for-your-business) . You can also download your old streams and edit them into shareable clips for platforms like Instagram and TikTok. Don’t forget to mention your Twitch account when you[cross-post this content](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cross-posting) .


### Focus on engagement and community


The ability to[engage with your audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/audience-engagement) in real time is one of the things that makes live content special. Interacting with your audience by asking questions, responding to comments, and welcoming newcomers can help you develop strong relationships.


Viewers may stick around longer to see if you answer their question or give them a shout-out. This can help boost your average concurrent viewer statistics and move you closer to affiliate eligibility.


Fostering a community outside of your streams is another way to build a loyal following. Many Twitch streamers use Discord to create a gathering place.


A dedicated Discord channel gives followers a way to interact with each other and connect with you throughout the day. This helps keep your content top of mind even when you’re not live.


## How to build a creator business beyond Twitch


- Sell merch
- Explore sponsorships and partnerships
- Join affiliate marketing programs
- Use a subscription or direct-tipping service


The very top Twitch streamers earn hundreds of thousands on a monthly basis, but[most people](https://financebuzz.com/how-much-twitch-streamers-make) make far less. If you have a dedicated fanbase, you may be able to supplement your income with other revenue streams related to your content.


These are some of the other ways Twitch streamers can make money:


### Sell merch


Consider[designing merch for Twitch](https://www.shopify.com/blog/make-merch-for-twitch) and selling it directly to your followers. You can earn money selling t-shirts and accessories, like hats and totes, with your channel logo, or specialty items related to your content. Try[making and selling merch](https://www.shopify.com/blog/make-sell-merch) at various price points. You could start with a few smaller items, like stickers or pins, available at a lower price point to test interest.


The[print-on-demand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/print-on-demand) business model is a low-risk, low-investment way to launch a custom[branded merchandise](https://www.shopify.com/blog/branding-merchandise) line. With this approach, you don’t need to handle shipping and logistics or bulk-order products before you know how well they’ll sell.


The[best print-on-demand companies](https://www.shopify.com/blog/print-on-demand-companies) include extensive product catalogs and intuitive drag-and-drop design tools. It’s easy to pick a product and add your[logo and branding](https://www.shopify.com/blog/logo-and-branding) without any specialized fashion or graphic design knowledge.


Top print-on-demand companies like[Printify](https://apps.shopify.com/printify) and[Gelato](https://apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand) are fully Shopify-compatible and available in the[Shopify App Store](https://apps.shopify.com/search?q=print%20on%20demand) .


### Explore sponsorships and partnerships


For many creators, brand deals are more lucrative than streaming.[Creators can earn income](https://www.shopify.com/blog/get-paid-to-create-content) by partnering with brands for sponsorships or advertising opportunities. To start looking for brand deals, make an[influencer media kit](https://www.shopify.com/blog/influencer-media-kit) and reach out to companies and agencies. You can also join a creator platform like[Shopify Collabs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-get-started-with-shopify-collabs) to let companies know you’re open to partnerships.


### Join affiliate marketing programs


[Content creators](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-a-content-creator) earn affiliate income by promoting other products or services. This typically involves forming an affiliate agreement with a company and sharing custom discount codes or tracking links with your followers. Businesses track traffic and sales associated with your account, and creators earn an[affiliate commission](https://www.shopify.com/blog/affiliate-commission) , or portion of the revenue.


### Use a subscription or direct-tipping service


Use a platform like Ko-fi or Patreon to accept direct payments from fans. Fan payments can be one-time tips or recurring contributions. Providing special rewards or exclusive content perks for platform followers may help encourage subscriptions.


## Twitch Affiliate FAQ


### Do Twitch Affiliates get paid?


The Affiliate Program is Twitch’s entry-level[monetization](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-monetization) program. Twitch Affiliates can earn income from paid subscriptions, ad revenue, and Bits. Channels become eligible for payouts once earnings exceed $50.


### How do I get into Twitch Affiliate?


The Twitch Affiliate program is available to creators with a minimum of 25 followers, four hours of streams, four active streaming days, and an average of three concurrent viewers per stream. If your channel meets these requirements, Twitch will invite you to join the affiliate program.


### Do Twitch Affiliates pay taxes?


Yes. Affiliates are still subject to tax obligations. Streamers must report and pay taxes on revenue generated on Twitch. This includes earnings from ad revenue, subscriptions, and Bits.
